headline: Nobody quit and the surface works (visual 7.4, Ruth and Priya recommend at 7, the truth table is the best part), but the game stopped asking questions: from month 3 everyone found that Accept all plus Execute was right, so agency (6.3) and replay (5.8) lag and the weighted recommend is flat at 6.2. Trust is the second drag: numbers and lines contradict or repeat, and several registered findings came back (eleven registry matches, one confirmed regression of RS-001-5, the desk advisor cards).

loved.what: The reveal, especially the truth table against the real world, the grade and seals, and a clear way back (RS-004)
Result cards with a big number, stamps, quote and newspaper; scenes that look like a real game
Forecasts and score breakdowns that say why every number moved, and warnings that name the mission it would break
Seed codes and Replay same opening: the same seed gives the same result

patterns.title: Accept all autopilot: nothing to decide after month 3
patterns.detail: Everyone guessed 'answer the crisis, skip the rest' and was right; capital sat unspent at the cap; crises answered unread; Olivia and Sam won on picks.

patterns.title: Advisor cards collapse to one letter per line (regression of RS-001-5)
patterns.detail: Desk 'Your advisors suggest' unreadable at every width from month 2; the guard only covered the Map strip.

patterns.title: Map mode hides the story and loses the player
patterns.detail: Crisis text missing, risky orders accepted unread, Add not confirmed, flips back to Desk, Map switch buried on phones, verbs differ from the desk.

patterns.title: Numbers and words contradict
patterns.detail: Mission strip vs report, verdict 5 of 5 vs 4, 13 orders for 1, moments under the wrong heading, 0 before counting, a FAILED order nobody gave.

patterns.title: Repeated and boilerplate lines
patterns.detail: Same reply from every leader, reused quotes, Court Iran monthly, staff courting a relation at -99, generic templates after the war ended.

patterns.title: Plausibility breaks the spell
patterns.detail: 1990 Iraq nuclear program and outbreak, Australia spying on China, one order ending the Ukraine war in month 3, seat counts for one-party states.

patterns.title: Phone reveal: sound button on Main menu and Skip
patterns.detail: Side effect of the RS-004 fix; tapping Skip leaves the reveal.

patterns.title: Layout seams and overlaps
patterns.detail: Labels over headlines, tablet rail overlap, truncated header, stamps over labels, reused crisis art.

patterns.title: Newcomers still meet homework
patterns.detail: Goal text with '-90+', unfamiliar names the i chips do not reach, no consequence line before accepting a meeting.

patterns.title: Play a seed is hard to find and use
patterns.detail: First tap failed, field hidden until tapped, the disabled button beside Today's crisis looks like the real one.

patterns.title: Which answer did I pick?
patterns.detail: No clear selected state on crisis answers; headings do not respond, cards do not look pressable.

patterns.title: Way back works, labels are muddy
patterns.detail: New game vs New world vs Replay, a label that looks like a button, Compare runs greyed; one big Play again was asked for twice.

patterns.title: Reveal polish
patterns.detail: Score 0 before counting, static on a wide stream, share buttons below the footer, stages 4 to 8 are homework for a teen, jargon in the truth table.

patterns.title: One vocabulary, not yet
patterns.detail: Cabinet pick vs Recommended, staff proposals, Hostile vs lamentable, Accept vs Add.

patterns.title: Replay a choice and compare, in the session
patterns.detail: Branch exists in Saved games but nobody found it from the debrief; what should I do differently?

surprises: The simplest path (Accept all, Execute) was the right answer in most months, and the more the game made that easy the less any persona felt clever.
Leo's deliberate war on Japan was the best clip of the round: a wild move with a clear warning and loud consequences is the strongest argument for the consequence work in iteration 2.
Noah (a teen) found Play a seed easiest and clarity hardest: the entry works, the goal text does not.
Eight of nine personas reached the reveal or their stop point without a single quit, yet the weighted recommend did not move from 6.3.
environment: Build d70608a (code as of 9624de4); the full verify gate passed but missed the desk advisor-card regression because its guard covered only the Map strip. Control seeds were fixed for the first time (D-59). Drivers sometimes failed the first click on 'Play a seed' while the globe was turning, which may overstate F-03-10 (QA notes the field itself looks like text). Several customer-reported bugs are not yet QA-reproduced.
